zh: 帝思念舅氏不已。
literal: The emperor thought of his maternal kin without cease.
idiomatic: The emperor could not stop thinking of his maternal kin.

zh: 暢尚幼，景初末，以暢為射聲校尉，加散騎常侍，又特為起大第，車駕親自臨之。
literal: Chang was still young; at the end of Jingchu he was made Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound and additionally Regular Attendant; a great mansion was specially built for him, and the imperial carriage personally visited it.
idiomatic: Chang was still young. At the end of Jingchu he was made Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound and Regular Attendant. A great mansion was specially built for him, and the emperor personally visited it.

zh: 又於其后園為像母起觀廟，名其里曰渭陽里，以追思母氏也。
literal: Also in the empress's rear garden a viewing temple was built for Xiang's mother; the lane was named Weiyang Lane, to recall and think of the maternal clan.
idiomatic: In the empress's rear garden a viewing temple was also built for Xiang's mother. The lane was named Weiyang Lane in remembrance of the maternal clan.

zh: 嘉平三年251年正月，暢薨，追贈車騎將軍，諡曰恭侯；
literal: In the first month of the third year of Jiaping (251 CE), Chang died; posthumously he was granted General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the posthumous title Marquis Gong;
idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaping 3 (251 CE), Chang died. He was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the posthumous title Marquis Gong;

zh: 子紹嗣。
literal: his son Shao succeeded.
idiomatic: his son Shao succeeded.

zh: 太和六年，明帝愛女淑薨，追封諡淑為平原懿公主，為之立廟。
literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, Ming-di's beloved daughter Shu died; posthumously she was enfeoffed and titled Princess Yi of Pingyuan, and a temple was built for her.
idiomatic: In Taihe 6, Ming-di's beloved daughter Shu died. She was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess Yi of Pingyuan, and a temple was built for her.

zh: 取后亡從孫黃與合葬，追封黃列侯，以夫人郭氏從弟德為之後，承甄氏姓，封德為平原侯，襲公主爵。
literal: The empress's deceased grandnephew Huang was taken to be buried with her; Huang was posthumously enfeoffed as a full marquis; Lady Guo's younger cousin De was made his heir, took the Zhen surname, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyuan, and inherited the princess's title.
idiomatic: The empress's deceased grandnephew Huang was buried with her and posthumously enfeoffed as a full marquis. Lady Guo's younger cousin De was made his heir, took the Zhen surname, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyuan, and inherited the princess's title.

zh: 孫盛曰：於禮，婦人既無封爵之典，況於孩末，而可建以大邑乎？
literal: Sun Sheng said: By ritual, women already have no norm of enfeoffment and titles—how much less a child in infancy; could one establish a great fief for such a case?
idiomatic: Sun Sheng said: "By ritual, women have no norm of enfeoffment and titles. How much less an infant child—could one establish a great fief in such a case?"

zh: 德自異族，援繼非類，匪功匪親，而襲母爵，違情背典，於此為甚。
literal: De came from a different clan; to pull in and continue an unsuitable line, neither by merit nor by kinship, yet to inherit a mother's title—this violates feeling and turns against the canon; in this matter the offense is extreme.
idiomatic: De came from a different clan. To install him as heir without merit or kinship, yet have him inherit a mother's title, violates both feeling and canon—and here the offense was extreme.

zh: 陳群雖抗言，楊阜引事比並，然皆不能極陳先王之禮，明封建繼嗣之義，忠至之辭，猶有闕乎！
literal: Although Chen Qun spoke out boldly and Yang Fu cited parallel cases, neither could fully set forth the rites of the former kings or clarify the meaning of enfeoffment and succession; their words of utmost loyalty still had gaps!
idiomatic: Although Chen Qun spoke out boldly and Yang Fu cited parallel cases, neither fully set forth the rites of the former kings or clarified the meaning of enfeoffment and succession. Even their most loyal remonstrance left something unsaid!

zh: 詩云：「赫赫師尹，民具爾瞻。」
literal: The Odes say: "Splendid is the master minister; the people all look to you."
idiomatic: The Odes say, "Splendid is the master minister; the people all look to you."

zh: 宰輔之職，其可略哉！
literal: The duty of chief ministers—can it be treated lightly!
idiomatic: The duty of chief ministers—can it be treated lightly!

zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：德字彥孫。
literal: Accounts of the Lords of Jin says: De's style was Yansun.
idiomatic: Accounts of the Lords of Jin says De's style was Yansun.

zh: 司馬景王輔政，以女妻德。
literal: When Sima Jingwang held regency, he gave his daughter to De in marriage.
idiomatic: When Sima Jingwang held regency, he gave his daughter to De in marriage.

zh: 妻早亡，文王復以女繼室，即京兆長公主。
literal: The wife died early; King Wen again gave a daughter as a successor wife, namely the Princess Chang of Jingzhao.
idiomatic: When the wife died early, King Wen again gave a daughter as a successor wife—the Princess Chang of Jingzhao.

zh: 景、文二王欲自結於郭后，是以頻繁為婚。
literal: The two kings Jing and Wen wished to bind themselves to Empress Guo, and therefore repeatedly contracted marriages.
idiomatic: The two kings Jing and Wen wished to bind themselves to Empress Guo, and therefore repeatedly contracted marriages.

zh: 德雖無才學，而恭謹謙順。
literal: Although De had no talent or learning, he was reverent, careful, modest, and compliant.
idiomatic: Although De had no talent or learning, he was reverent, careful, modest, and compliant.

zh: 甄溫字仲舒，與郭建及德等皆后族，以事宜見寵。
literal: Zhen Wen's style was Zhongshu; he, Guo Jian, De, and the rest were all empress kin and were favored for affairs of state.
idiomatic: Zhen Wen's style was Zhongshu. He, Guo Jian, De, and the rest were all empress kin and were favored for affairs of state.

zh: 咸熙初，封郭建為臨渭縣公，德廣安縣公，邑皆千八百戶。
literal: At the beginning of Xianxi, Guo Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Linwei County and De as Duke of Guang'an County, each with eighteen hundred households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianxi, Guo Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Linwei County and De as Duke of Guang'an County, each with eighteen hundred households.

zh: 溫本國侯，進為輔國大將軍，加侍中，領射聲校尉，德鎮軍大將軍。
literal: Wen was originally a marquis of the founding state; he was advanced to General Who Assists the State, additionally made Palace Attendant, and put in charge as Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound; De was made General Who Guards the Army.
idiomatic: Wen was originally a marquis of the founding state. He was advanced to General Who Assists the State, additionally made Palace Attendant, and put in charge as Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound. De was made General Who Guards the Army.

zh: 泰始元年，晉受禪，加建、德、溫三人位特進。
literal: In the first year of Taishi, when Jin received the abdication, Jian, De, and Wen were all advanced to Special Advance.
idiomatic: In Taishi 1, when Jin received the abdication, Jian, De, and Wen were all advanced to Special Advance.

zh: 德為人貞素，加以世祖姊夫，是以遂貴當世。
literal: De as a man was upright and plain; added to this, he was the brother-in-law of Shizu, and therefore came to be honored in his age.
idiomatic: De was upright and plain by nature, and as the brother-in-law of Shizu he came to be honored in his age.

zh: 德暮年官更轉為宗正，遷侍中。
literal: In De's later years his office was changed to Director of the Imperial Clan, and he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: In De's later years he was made Director of the Imperial Clan and transferred to Palace Attendant.

zh: 太康中，大司馬齊王攸當之籓，德與左衛將軍王濟共諫請，時人嘉之。
literal: In Taikang, when Grand Marshal Prince of Qi You was about to go to his fief, De and Left Guard General Wang Ji jointly remonstrated and petitioned; men of the time praised this.
idiomatic: In Taikang, when Grand Marshal Prince of Qi You was about to go to his fief, De and Left Guard General Wang Ji jointly remonstrated and petitioned, and men of the time praised them.

zh: 世祖以此望德，由此出德為大鴻臚，加侍中、光祿大夫，尋疾薨，贈中軍大將軍，開府侍中如故，諡恭公，子喜嗣。
literal: Shizu on this account looked askance at De; for this reason De was sent out as Grand Herald, additionally made Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; soon he died of illness; posthumously he was granted General of the Central Army, with an office and Palace Attendant as before, given the posthumous title Duke Gong, and his son Xi succeeded.
idiomatic: Shizu on this account looked askance at De and sent him out as Grand Herald, additionally making him Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Soon he died of illness. He was posthumously made General of the Central Army with an office and Palace Attendant as before, given the posthumous title Duke Gong, and his son Xi succeeded.

zh: 喜精粹有器美，歷中書郎、右衛將軍、侍中，位至輔國大將軍，加散騎常侍。
literal: Xi was refined and possessed fine capacity; he passed through Palace Secretary, Right Guard General, and Palace Attendant, reaching the rank of General Who Assists the State and additionally Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Xi was refined and possessed fine capacity. He served as Palace Secretary, Right Guard General, and Palace Attendant, reaching the rank of General Who Assists the State and Regular Attendant.

zh: 喜與國姻親，而經趙王倫、齊王冏事故，能不豫際會，良由其才短，然亦以退靜免之。
literal: Xi was related by marriage to the state, yet through the affairs of Prince of Zhao Lun and Prince of Qi Jiong he was able not to take part in those encounters—likely because his talent was short, yet he was also spared by retiring into quiet.
idiomatic: Xi was related by marriage to the state, yet through the affairs of Prince of Zhao Lun and Prince of Qi Jiong he was able to stay out of those encounters—likely because his talent was limited, but also because retiring into quiet spared him.

zh: 青龍中，又封后從兄子毅及像弟三人，皆為列侯。
literal: In Qinglong, the empress's cousin's son Yi and Xiang's three younger brothers were again enfeoffed, all as full marquises.
idiomatic: In Qinglong, the empress's cousin's son Yi and Xiang's three younger brothers were again enfeoffed, all as full marquises.

zh: 毅數上疏陳時政，官至越騎校尉。
literal: Yi repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth current policy and reached the office of Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.
idiomatic: Yi repeatedly submitted memorials on current policy and reached the office of Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.

zh: 嘉平中，复封暢子二人為列侯。
literal: In Jiaping, Chang's two sons were again enfeoffed as full marquises.
idiomatic: In Jiaping, Chang's two sons were again enfeoffed as full marquises.

zh: 后兄儼孫女為齊王皇后，后父已沒，封后母為廣樂鄉君。
literal: The empress's elder brother Yan's granddaughter became empress to the Prince of Qi; the empress's father was already dead, so the empress's mother was enfeoffed as Lady of Guangle Township.
idiomatic: The empress's elder brother Yan's granddaughter became empress to the Prince of Qi. The empress's father was already dead, so her mother was enfeoffed as Lady of Guangle Township.

zh: 文德郭皇后，安平廣宗人也。
literal: Empress Wen-De, née Guo, was a native of Guangzong in Anping.
idiomatic: Empress Wen-De of the Guo clan came from Guangzong in Anping.

zh: 祖世長吏。
literal: For generations her forebears were chief clerks.
idiomatic: For generations her forebears had served as chief clerks.

zh: 《魏書》曰：父永，官至南郡太守，諡敬侯。
literal: The Book of Wei says: her father Yong reached the office of Administrator of Nan Commandery and was given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
idiomatic: The Book of Wei says her father Yong reached the office of Administrator of Nan Commandery and received the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

zh: 母姓董氏，即堂陽君，生三男二女：長男浮，高唐令，次女昱，次即后，后弟都，弟成。
literal: Her mother was of the Dong clan, namely Lady Tangyang; she bore three sons and two daughters: the eldest son Fu, Magistrate of Gaotang; the second daughter Yu; next was the empress; the empress's younger brothers Du and Cheng.
idiomatic: Her mother was of the Dong clan, namely Lady Tangyang. She bore three sons and two daughters: the eldest son Fu, Magistrate of Gaotang; the second daughter Yu; next the empress; and the empress's younger brothers Du and Cheng.

zh: 后以漢中平元年三月乙卯生，生而有異常。
literal: The empress was born on the yimao day of the third month of the first year of Zhongping of Han; at birth there were unusual signs.
idiomatic: The empress was born on the yimao day of the third month of Han Zhongping 1; at birth there were unusual signs.

zh: 后少而父永奇之曰：「此乃吾女中王也。」
literal: When the empress was young her father Yong marveled at her, saying, "This is the king among my daughters."
idiomatic: When the empress was young her father Yong marveled at her, saying, "This is the king among my daughters."

zh: 遂以女王為字。
literal: Thereupon he took Nüwang as her style.
idiomatic: Thereupon he took Nüwang as her style.

zh: 早失二親，喪亂流離，沒在銅鞮侯家。
literal: She early lost both parents; in the chaos of mourning and disorder she was cast adrift and ended up in the household of the Marquis of Tongdi.
idiomatic: She early lost both parents. In the chaos of war and exile she ended up in the household of the Marquis of Tongdi.

zh: 太祖為魏公時，得入東宮。
literal: When the Grand Ancestor became Duke of Wei, she was able to enter the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor became Duke of Wei, she entered the Eastern Palace.

zh: 后有智數，時時有所獻納。
literal: The empress had wisdom and calculation and from time to time offered suggestions.
idiomatic: The empress was clever and from time to time offered suggestions.

zh: 文帝定為嗣，后有謀焉。
literal: When Wen-di was fixed as heir, the empress had a hand in the plan.
idiomatic: When Wen-di was fixed as heir, the empress had a hand in the plan.

zh: 太子即王位，后為夫人，及踐阼，為貴嬪。
literal: When the heir apparent took the royal title, the empress became Lady; when he ascended the throne, she became Honored Consort.
idiomatic: When the heir apparent took the royal title, she became Lady; when he ascended the throne, she became Honored Consort.

zh: 甄后之死，由后之寵也。
literal: Empress Zhen's death came from this empress's favor.
idiomatic: Empress Zhen's death came from this empress's favor.

zh: 黃初三年，將登后位，文帝欲立為后，中郎棧潛上疏曰：「在昔帝王之治天下，不惟外輔，亦有內助，治亂所由，盛衰從之。
literal: In the third year of Huangchu, as she was about to ascend the empress's seat, Wen-di wished to install her as empress; Palace Gentleman Stack Qian submitted a memorial, saying, "In former times when emperors and kings governed the realm, they relied not only on outer assistance but also on inner support; order and disorder arise from this, and rise and decline follow it."
idiomatic: In Huangchu 3, as she was about to ascend the empress's seat, Wen-di wished to install her as empress. Palace Gentleman Stack Qian submitted a memorial, saying, "In former times when emperors and kings governed the realm, they relied not only on outer assistance but also on inner support; order and disorder arise from this, and rise and decline follow it."

zh: 故西陵配黃，英娥降媯，並以賢明，流芳上世。
literal: Therefore Xiling was paired with Huang and the heroic maid descended to the Gui clan; all by sage wisdom and clarity, their fragrance flowed in upper ages.
idiomatic: Therefore Xiling was paired with Huang and the heroic maid descended to the Gui clan—all by sage wisdom and clarity, their fame flowed through upper ages.

zh: 桀奔南巢，禍階末喜；
literal: Jie fled to Southern Nest and disaster began with Mo Xi;
idiomatic: Jie fled to Southern Nest and disaster began with Mo Xi;

zh: 紂以砲烙，怡悅妲己。
literal: Zhou used the burning pillar and took delight in Daji.
idiomatic: Zhou used the burning pillar and took delight in Daji.

zh: 是以聖哲慎立元妃，必取先代世族之家，擇其令淑以統六宮，虔奉宗廟，陰教聿修。
literal: Therefore the sage and wise are careful in establishing the primary consort; they must take a house of hereditary clans of former ages, choose one who is good and virtuous to govern the six palaces, reverently serve the ancestral temple, and fully cultivate inner instruction.
idiomatic: Therefore the sage and wise are careful in establishing the primary consort. They must take a house of hereditary clans of former ages, choose one who is good and virtuous to govern the six palaces, reverently serve the ancestral temple, and fully cultivate inner instruction.

zh: 易曰：『家道正而天下定。』
literal: The Changes says, 'When the way of the family is correct, the realm is settled.'
idiomatic: The Changes says, "When the way of the family is correct, the realm is settled."

zh: 由內及外，先王之令典也。
literal: From inner to outer—this is the august norm of the former kings.
idiomatic: From inner to outer—this is the august norm of the former kings.

zh: 春秋書宗人釁夏云，無以妾為夫人之禮。
literal: The Spring and Autumn records the Director of the Clan performing the summer offering and says there is no rite for making a concubine a lady.
idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records the Director of the Clan performing the summer offering and says there is no rite for making a concubine a lady.

zh: 齊桓誓命於葵丘，亦曰『無以妾為妻』。
literal: Duke Huan of Qi swore his command at Kuqiu and likewise said, 'Do not take a concubine as wife.'
idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi swore his command at Kuqiu and likewise said, "Do not take a concubine as wife."

zh: 今后宮嬖寵，常亞乘輿。
literal: Now in the inner palace favored concubines often rank just below the imperial carriage.
idiomatic: Now in the inner palace favored concubines often rank just below the imperial carriage.

zh: 若因愛登后，使賤人暴貴，臣恐後世下陵上替，開張非度，亂自上起也。」
literal: If through affection one installs her as empress and makes a base person suddenly exalted, I fear that in later ages inferiors will encroach on superiors and the proper order will be overturned, irregular practices will be opened wide, and disorder will rise from above."
idiomatic: If through affection one installs her as empress and makes a base person suddenly exalted, I fear that in later ages inferiors will encroach on superiors, irregular practices will be opened wide, and disorder will rise from above."

zh: 文帝不從，遂立為皇后。
literal: Wen-di did not follow this and thereupon installed her as empress.
idiomatic: Wen-di did not follow this and installed her as empress.

zh: 《魏書》曰：后上表謝曰：「妾無皇、英釐降之節，又非姜、任思齊之倫，誠不足以假充女君之盛位，處中饋之重任。」
literal: The Book of Wei states: the empress submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Your handmaid lacks the virtue of Huang and Ying or the descending grace of Li; nor am I of the same order as Jiang and Ren in aspiring to equal virtue. Truly I am not sufficient to borrow and fill the exalted seat of the female sovereign or bear the heavy charge of the inner kitchen."
idiomatic: The Book of Wei says the empress submitted a memorial of thanks, saying, "Your handmaid lacks the virtue of Huang and Ying or the descending grace of Li, nor am I of the same order as Jiang and Ren in aspiring to equal virtue. Truly I am not fit to fill the exalted seat of the female sovereign or bear the heavy charge of the inner household."

zh: 后自在東宮，及即尊位，雖有異寵，心愈恭肅，供養永壽宮，以孝聞。
literal: From the time she was in the Eastern Palace until she reached the honored position, although she had special favor, her heart grew ever more reverent and solemn; she supported Yongshou Palace and was known for filial piety.
idiomatic: From the Eastern Palace until she reached the honored position, although she had special favor, her heart grew ever more reverent and solemn. She supported Yongshou Palace and was known for filial piety.

zh: 是時柴貴人亦有寵，后教訓獎導之。
literal: At that time Honored Lady Chai also had favor; the empress instructed, exhorted, and guided her.
idiomatic: At that time Honored Lady Chai also had favor, and the empress instructed, exhorted, and guided her.

zh: 后宮諸貴人時有過失，常彌覆之，有譴讓，輒為帝言其本末，帝或大有所怒，至為之頓首請罪，是以六宮無怨。
literal: When the various honored ladies of the inner palace at times had faults, she constantly covered them over; when there was reproof or censure, she would explain the whole matter to the emperor; the emperor might become greatly angry, even to the point that she would kowtow and plead guilt—thus the six palaces were without resentment.
idiomatic: When the various honored ladies of the inner palace at times had faults, she constantly covered them over. When there was reproof or censure, she would explain the whole matter to the emperor. The emperor might become greatly angry, even to the point that she would kowtow and plead guilt—thus the six palaces were without resentment.

zh: 性儉約，不好音樂，常慕漢明德馬后之為人。
literal: By nature she was frugal and restrained, disliked music, and constantly admired the conduct of Empress Ma the Bright and Virtuous of Han.
idiomatic: By nature she was frugal and restrained, disliked music, and constantly admired the conduct of Empress Ma the Bright and Virtuous of Han.
